change.author: nicktrn

findings.title: Backup code login can skip the password check
findings.body:
The password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new backup-code branch (line 131) never looks at `totpCode`. The credentials callback accepts arbitrary POST fields, so a request with a victim's email, any non-empty `totpCode` (e.g. "x") and a valid `backupCode` skips the password check (line 121). It then passes the backup-code branch and returns a user. A backup code alone, such as a leaked `cal-backup-codes.txt`, therefore logs in with no password and no TOTP.

The existing `totpCode` bypass still required a valid TOTP. The new branch needs only a static 40-bit code, and it ignores the junk `totpCode`. Make the password check run whenever `credentials.backupCode` is set. For example, change the condition at line 121 to `user.password && (!credentials.totpCode || credentials.backupCode)`. Alternatively, reject a request that sends both `totpCode` and `backupCode`.

findings.title: Dismissing the dialog on the backup-codes step loses the codes and leaves the settings page stale
findings.body: `/enable` has already turned 2FA on by the time the backup-codes step shows (line 135). The footer hides Cancel on that step, but the dialog still closes on Esc or an overlay click, because the parent's `onOpenChange` just toggles `open` (`apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64`). That path never calls `onEnable`, so `viewer.me` is not invalidated. The switch keeps showing 2FA as disabled while it is enabled server-side. The user may also never have saved the one-time codes. `step` stays at `DisplayBackupCodes`, since only the Close and Cancel buttons call `resetState`. Block dismissal while on this step, for example by ignoring `onOpenChange` there. Alternatively, run the Close handler (`resetState` plus `onEnable`) whenever the dialog closes on that step.

findings.title: Placeholder is uppercase but codes are lowercase hex and compared case-sensitively
findings.body: Codes are generated with `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, which is lowercase (`setup.ts:61`). The input placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX` (line 21), and comparison is `indexOf` with no case normalisation (`next-auth-options.ts:144`, `disable.ts:61`). A user who types the code in uppercase gets "Backup code is incorrect". Lowercase the input on both server paths, or change the placeholder.

findings.title: Component is named TwoFactor
findings.body: The default export is named `TwoFactor`, the same as `components/auth/TwoFactor.tsx`. Rename it to `BackupCode`, because the name shows up in stack traces and React devtools.

findings.title: missing_backup_codes message points to a feature that does not exist
findings.body: The message says "Please generate them in your settings". Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have `backupCodes = null`. `setup.ts:42-44` rejects setup when 2FA is already enabled. The only way to generate codes is to disable 2FA, which needs the TOTP they may have lost, and then re-enable it. No settings action generates codes. Either add a regenerate flow or reword the message.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: The code reads the decrypted list (line 139), finds the index, then writes back the whole re-encrypted list (line 149). Two concurrent logins with the same code can both pass the `indexOf` check before either write. Concurrent logins with two different codes can also overwrite each other, which restores one of the used codes. The rate limiter reduces this risk but does not close it. Consider a transaction or an optimistic check on the stored ciphertext, such as `updateMany` with `where: { id, backupCodes: user.backupCodes }`, and fail if the count is 0.

findings.title: Lost-access mode and entered values survive Cancel or close
findings.body: `twoFactorLostAccess` and the form values are reset only on a successful disable (lines 60-61). `onCancel` and Esc leave the modal in backup-code mode, with any typed backup code or password still in the form. The parent component stays mounted (`two-factor-auth.tsx:74`), so the next open shows the stale state. Reset the state when the dialog closes.

findings.title: Core backup-code behaviour is untested
findings.body: The new e2e coverage only checks the download, copy and close buttons. Nothing tests logging in with a backup code, single-use consumption, a wrong code, or disabling 2FA with a backup code. The TODO on line 12 acknowledges the gap, but those paths hold the security-relevant logic (for example the password-bypass issue in `next-auth-options.ts`). The FIXME added at lines 50-51 describes an existing weak assertion and is unrelated to this change.

contracts.action: Login with a backup code (credentials authorize)
contracts.equivalent_path: TOTP branch in the same function (lines 157-187), preceded by the password check at lines 121-129
contracts.before_after: The TOTP path checks the password unless `totpCode` is set, then validates the TOTP. The backup path sits under the same password guard (`!credentials.totpCode`). It does not validate `totpCode`, so a junk `totpCode` skips the password check. On success it nulls the used code and re-encrypts the list. Errors are thrown as ErrorCode values, which login.tsx maps to messages.
contracts.visible_effect: The login page shows "Backup code is incorrect" or "No backup codes found", or signs the user in.
contracts.failure_mode: Password bypass with a junk totpCode plus a valid backupCode. The code consumption is not atomic. A decrypt or parse failure throws a raw error, which login shows as the generic message.

contracts.action: Enable 2FA now shows backup codes after TOTP confirmation
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous flow called onEnable() right after /enable returned 200
contracts.before_after: Before, the modal closed and `viewer.me` was invalidated. Now it moves to the DisplayBackupCodes step, and `onEnable` runs only from the Close button. Codes come from the setup response and are held in React state. The download URL is a blob URL.
contracts.visible_effect: The user sees the codes and can copy or download them. The settings switch updates only after Close.
contracts.failure_mode: Esc or an overlay click calls the parent's `onOpenChange` toggle. 2FA stays enabled server-side, the UI stays stale, and the codes are lost. The blob URL is revoked only on a later setup call.

contracts.equivalent_path: The TOTP branch at lines 69-100 of the same handler
contracts.before_after: The password check runs first for CAL users, then either the backup-code or the TOTP verification. On success the update now also sets `backupCodes: null`. The backup code is not consumed on its own, which is fine because all codes are wiped.
contracts.visible_effect: The modal shows an error message, or closes and the switch updates.
contracts.failure_mode: A non-string `backupCode` throws a TypeError at `replaceAll` and returns a 500. Legacy users with null codes get MissingBackupCodes.

contracts.action: Setup generates and stores backup codes and returns them in the response
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing secret generation and encrypted storage at lines 58 and 70
contracts.before_after: Codes are encrypted with the same key and stored together with the secret while `twoFactorEnabled` is false. Every setup call regenerates them. The plaintext codes are returned to the client before the TOTP is confirmed.
contracts.visible_effect: The codes are shown only after /enable succeeds.
contracts.failure_mode: Abandoned setups leave unused encrypted codes in the table. They are overwritten on the next setup. They are only usable once 2FA is enabled.

summary:
I found one blocker and one fix, plus several smaller points.

- **Blocker:** the backup-code login path in `next-auth-options.ts` can skip the password check. Line 121 only verifies the password when `totpCode` is empty, and the new branch at line 131 never looks at `totpCode`. A junk `totpCode` plus a valid backup code logs in without the password.
- **Fix:** closing the enable dialog with Esc or an overlay click on the backup-codes step loses the codes. It also leaves the settings switch stale, because `onEnable` is never called.
- **Smaller points:**
  - The placeholder is uppercase but the codes are lowercase hex.
  - The `missing_backup_codes` message points to a settings action that does not exist.
  - Backup-code consumption is not atomic.
  - The disable modal keeps its state after Cancel.
  - `BackupCode.tsx` exports a component named `TwoFactor`.
  - There is no e2e coverage of login or disable with a backup code.

I read all 16 files in full and ran nothing."
